first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 6,917,021 shares = 16.23% of float, 7.4 days to cover, record date 2026-10-15 (published 2026-10-26), up 14.4% from 6,046,389 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/BBNX/short-interest). No skew available: the baseline's option arm returned no_paired_strikes for the 2026-11-20 expiry. One undated search snippet claimed options imply about +/-20%; it has no source and is not used. Tape: +21.36% over 5 sessions, +10.92% over 20, -32.7% from the 52-week high, +143% off the low; spot $21.53 against the $17.25 September offering price. Beta about 3.4 (MarketBeat).

evidence.text: On the Q2 call (2026-07-29) the CFO said 'Q3 will be a step up from Q2' in new patient starts, said the 2025 quarterly shape is 'generally consistent with what we're expecting in 2026', and said the 20+ territories added in H1 begin generating demand about one quarter after onboarding. In 2025 Q3 revenue was +17.5% q/q ($23.2m to $27.25m). The $34.59m Q3 consensus implies only +8% q/q and +27% y/y, after Q2 grew +38% y/y and beat consensus ($32.0m vs ~$31.4-31.5m). My read: Q3 revenue lands ~$35-35.5m, about 2% above the bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have stopped paying: Q2 2026 beat by about 2% with a GM guide raise and the stock fell 5.93%; Q1 2026 beat with a $1m guide raise and it fell 0.57%. Earlier beats paid: Q3 2025 revenue $27.25m vs $23.92m consensus (+14%) and the stock rose 10.34%. The -37% print on 2026-01-08 was a miss on new patient starts.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the street had taken management's 2025-shape comment literally, Q3 consensus would sit near $37m (Q2 x 1.175), not $34.6m, and the FY consensus would sit above the guide midpoint, not on it. The 21% five-day run-up partly prices a beat, which is why the size is small.
evidence.independence: Q3 2025 base ($27.25m, 5,334 new patient starts) is from the company's own Q3 2025 release: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35739606/beta-bionics-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results-and-raises-full-year-2025-guidance . The Q2 beat size is from https://www.drugdeliverybusiness.com/beta-bionics-q2-beats-2026-growth/ . The q/q guidance shares a transcript with finding 2.

evidence.text: The CFO said Q2 2026 pharmacy-channel (PBP) revenue was 'driven by what I call a stocking dynamic from our pharmacy customers' and that PBP revenue 'can be pretty dramatically impacted based on ordering patterns'. Q2 PBP revenue was $11.6m (+153% y/y) against $10.7m in Q1. DME revenue grew only 9% to $20.4m and was flat-to-down sequentially versus Q3 2025's $21.0m base. A Q3 destock in PBP could leave revenue at or below $34.6m even if new patient starts rise.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior PBP destock quarter to read. The January 2026 starts miss was punished at -37%, so a top-line shortfall on this name is sized by the market far above a beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: The previews and aggregators carry the $32.0m headline and the +38%; the stocking qualifier sits in the Q&A, not the release. If it were priced, the Q3 bar would show a PBP step-down and the stock would not have run 21% into the print.
evidence.independence: Shares a transcript with finding 1, but reads a different line: the timing of pharmacy orders, not patient starts. Q2 channel split from https://www.drugdeliverybusiness.com/beta-bionics-q2-beats-2026-growth/ and https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/beta-bionics-q2-earnings-call-highlights . Both findings can be true together, and they partly offset.

evidence.text: The FY2026 revenue guide of $131-136m was only reiterated on 2026-07-29 despite a Q2 beat. It implies H2 growth of +20-29% y/y against +46% in H1 ($59.6m vs $40.8m). A Q3 near $35m would make the $131m floor look conservative and set up a low-end raise, as the company did in Q1 ($130-135m to $131-136m). The FY consensus ($133.15m) sits at the guide midpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 $1m guide raise met -0.57%. The Q2 2026 reiteration plus a GM guide raise met -5.93%. The Q3 2025 guide raise met +10.34%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the FY consensus already sits at the midpoint, not the top. A raise to $133-137m or more would move the street above midpoint. A cut, for example from a PBP destock, is the downside tail.
evidence.independence: The Q1 raise is from the company release: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1433060/beta-bionics-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-raises-full-year-2026-guidance

evidence.text: The stock ran +21.4% in the five sessions into the print with no company news; on 2026-10-26 it was up 9.9% on volume about 48% below average, and MarketBeat named no catalyst. That puts spot at $21.53, 25% above the $17.25 September offering price. Short interest is 16.2% of float with 7.4 days to cover, and it rose 14% in the first half of October. The run-up raises the bar the release has to clear on a name that sold its last two beats. The crowded short is a squeeze mechanism that limits the downside.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior case of a 20%+ pre-print run-up in the eight baseline prints. The two most recent beats were sold (-0.57%, -5.93%).
evidence.why_not_priced: This is positioning, so it is the price itself. The question is whether a modest beat is enough after +21%. If the run-up had been a reaction to news, there would be a dated catalyst. There is none, and the volume was thin.
evidence.independence: Short interest from https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/BBNX/short-interest (record date 2026-10-15). The run-up is from the sealed baseline.

evidence.text: Peer read: Insulet cut its US outlook on 2026-08-05, attributing about one third of the cut to a slow start in new customer starts and pricing/mix. Tandem's Q2 2026 US pump shipments were about 22,000 against about 21,000 a year earlier (+5%). The US pump market was soft into H2. Neither peer has reported Q3: Tandem reports 2026-11-05 and Insulet has not reported.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: BBNX beat in Q2 2026 in the same soft peer quarter (Insulet cut, Tandem flat). Its MDI-conversion mix (about 69% of starts) has decoupled it from peer pump-switch volumes.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is a two-month-old proxy that BBNX already printed through, so the size is small.
evidence.independence: Proxy, not a company number. Tandem Q2 2026 is from https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3712557/tndm-q2-deep-dive-pharmacy-channel-gains-and-pipeline-execution-amid-margin-recovery

evidence.text: Gross margin guidance was raised to 58.5-59.5% on 2026-07-29, after Q1 printed 59.5% helped by what management called 'a couple of one-time gross margin tailwinds'. The rising PBP mix (37-39% of starts) is margin-accretive. A further raise or a print at the top of the range is possible but secondary to starts and revenue.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 GM raise came with a -5.93% reaction, so the line has not paid on its own.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the range was already raised and margin is not the line this name trades on.
evidence.independence: Q1 one-time tailwind comment: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1433060/beta-bionics-announces-first-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-raises-full-year-2026-guidance (company release and call summary). Shares a document with finding 3.

evidence.text: The 3D Intelligence algorithm 510(k) was submitted and is pending; the 2026-09-14 8-K says iLet 3D commercialisation is expected by the end of 2026, subject to FDA clearance. No clearance has been reported as of 2026-10-27, so a clearance or a timing update on the call is possible.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Mint FDA clearance (2026-09-14) lifted the stock: it traded $20.37 (+5.9%) on 2026-09-16 despite a $150m offering priced at $17.25.
evidence.why_not_priced: The timing is unknown. A clearance announced with the print would be new; a slip past year-end would be a mild negative. It is binary and has no date, so the size is small.
evidence.independence: Pending status was confirmed by HCPLive and RTTNews coverage of the Mint clearance: https://www.rttnews.com/3690706/beta-bionics-fda-clearance-of-mint-sets-stage-for-2027-patch-pump-launch.aspx

evidence.text: FDA overhang: a 2026-01-28 warning letter called the iLet dosing software and ACE pump 'adulterated'. The prospectus of 2026-09-15 cites a post-market surveillance order and 'four open recalls'. On the Q2 call the CEO said complaint handling and post-market surveillance were 'heavily revised'. A close-out or a new observation would be news on the call. No new recall initiated in Aug-Oct 2026 was found.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 4.9% on 2026-02-24, when the FDA published the warning letter (per the class-action complaint).
evidence.why_not_priced: The status is in the price as an open overhang. Neither direction is evidenced, so the size is zero.
evidence.independence: Warning letter coverage: https://www.drugdeliverybusiness.com/beta-bionics-receives-fda-warning-letter/ . The remediation comment is from the Q2 transcript, https://www.webull.com/news/15364580160791552

evidence.text: Financing: a $150.0m offering was priced 2026-09-15 at $17.25 (7.65m shares plus 1.04m pre-funded warrants, about 52.6m shares outstanding after). Proceeds fund the Mint patch-pump launch (full US launch Q1 2027, capacity for at least 1.5m disposables in 2027) and manufacturing expansion. With June 30 cash of $225.2m this removes the funding question. The money buys a dated launch, not a going-concern fix.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock traded higher after pricing (+5.9% on 2026-09-16) and now sits 25% above the deal price.
evidence.why_not_priced: Priced. It is filed so the panel sees that the balance sheet is not a print risk. 2027 opex for the Mint launch could come up on the call.
evidence.independence: Mint launch timing from the 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001674632/000119312526392088/d153052d8k.htm

evidence.text: The FY2026 revenue guide of $90-92m, reiterated 2026-07-29, needs H2 revenue of $46.7-48.7m (H1 was $43.3m). Management guided Q3 sequentially down (U.S. typically down; outside the U.S. flat to down a few %) and consensus has Q3 at $22.0m. That leaves Q4 at $24.7-26.7m against $22.6m in Q4 2025, i.e. +9-18% y/y. China shipments are not expected until early 2027, and management's own stated exit rate is 'at or close to double digits' (about $24.9m). That exit rate reaches only the bottom of the range. FY consensus of $90.88m sits in the lower half, so a narrowing to the low end or a trim to about $89-90m is the likelier guidance outcome than a reiteration of the midpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line has driven this name's largest moves. On 2025-07-30 a FY guide cut brought -41.6%. On 2025-11-12, after Q3 revenue had been pre-released, the outlook reaction was -18.9%. On 2026-07-29 a beat plus reiterated guide brought +28.8%. On 2026-03-04, with the first 2026 guide in line with consensus, the stock moved +11.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: FY consensus is $90.88m, inside the range, and the stock rallied from $1.27 to above $2 after the reiteration. If the market already expected a trim, consensus would sit at or below $90m and the post-Q2 rally would have fully round-tripped. Price is $1.975, still 55% above the pre-Q2 level.
evidence.independence: Uses the same company documents as the Q3 reported-quarter finding (Q2 8-K and Q2 call). The H1 figure, guide and China timing are from the Q2 8-K and 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001127537/000112753726000035/lung2q26earningsrelease072.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001127537/000112753726000039/lung-20260630.htm). The Q4 2025 comparison of $22.6m is from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1127537/000112753726000003/lung4q25earningsrelease030.htm. This is arithmetic, not a counterparty confirmation.

evidence.text: Q3 revenue looks in line to slightly below the $22.0m consensus. Applying management's guided seasonality to Q2 ($22.8m; U.S. $14.2m, international $8.6m) gives U.S. about $13.3-13.8m and international about $8.3-8.6m, a total of about $21.4-22.1m. Q3 2025 was $21.5m. On the Q2 call an analyst noted consensus models may need to shift revenue from Q3 to Q4, so the company has already told the market to expect a soft Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have been bought. Q2 2026 revenue of $22.76m against $22.24-22.39m brought +28.8%. Q1 2026 ($20.6m, a slight beat) brought +6.7%. Q4 2025 ($22.6m, beat) brought +11.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The company guided the seasonal dip, and the item lands inside what was guided. It is kept small because the aggregator consensus of $22.0m implies only about -3.5% sequential, which is at the generous end of the guided seasonality.
evidence.independence: Same Q2 call document as the guidance finding. The Q2 split is from the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001127537/000112753726000035/lung2q26earningsrelease072.htm). Q3 2025 revenue of $21.5m is from the 2025-10-27 prelim (https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/pulmonx-reports-preliminary-q3-revenue-21-5m-consensus-20-78m-thefly).

evidence.text: The cost and margin line likely beats again. Gross margin was a record 78% in Q2 against 72% a year earlier. The FY opex guide was cut to $109-111m (including about $15m SBC) from $113-115m (about $21m SBC) in March. Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 39% to $5.1m and EPS beat for the 8th straight quarter. With FY GM guided at only about 76%, Q3 EPS of -$0.26 against Q2's -$0.24 looks conservative unless revenue misses badly.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 EPS beat ($-0.24 vs $-0.28), paired with record GM, was bought +28.8%. Benzinga records 8 consecutive EPS beats, so the market expects one.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced, since the beat streak is visible. What may not be priced is that the 76% FY GM guide implies H2 GM of about 74% after two 78% quarters. Management said GM stays at or above 75% even after China returns, so the GM guide looks padded. A third 78% print would be a quality beat that a -$0.26 consensus does not reflect.
evidence.independence: The opex guide change is from the March 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1127537/000112753726000003/lung4q25earningsrelease030.htm) against the July release. The beat streak is from Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/LUNG/earnings-forecasts). Different documents, same company.

evidence.text: There is no financing cliff in the window. Under the Perceptive term loan, the minimum trailing-12-month revenue covenant is flat at $85.0m through 2028, including the 2026-09-30 and 2026-12-31 test dates (Credit Agreement s.10.02). TTM revenue at Q2 was about $87.5m, minimum liquidity is $4.0m, and cash was $55.8m against a guided 2026 burn of about $23m. The 10-Q carries no substantial-doubt language. The money funds the burn while opex falls, not a ramp. Answer: the facility is neutral, with no covenant pressure.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print where financing was the line. The 2026-03-04 print, which carried the facility announcement, moved +11.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: At about an $85m market cap, roughly 1x sales, part of the discount is distress risk. The covenant schedule sits only in a 755KB exhibit, and a market that had read it would not price a near-term covenant or dilution tail. The size is small because a Q3 print does not change it.
evidence.independence: The 10-Q states compliance at 2026-06-30 and the going-concern basis (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001127537/000112753726000039/lung-20260630.htm).

evidence.text: HCA's Q3 2026 release, today, shows same-facility outpatient surgeries -3.7% and inpatient surgeries -1.4% y/y, against +1.1% for outpatient in Q3 2025. HCA tied this partly to a payer-mix shift toward uninsured patients after exchange coverage losses. It is a broad hospital-procedure series covering the quarter Pulmonx is reporting.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction for this proxy. U.S. Zephyr procedure volumes were the cause of the 2025 guide cut (-41.6%).
evidence.why_not_priced: It was released this morning, after the Q3 consensus formed, and nobody maps HCA surgery counts onto an $85m valve company. Transmission is weak: Zephyr patients are mostly elderly Medicare patients with severe emphysema, while HCA's shortfall is concentrated in uninsured and low-acuity categories.
evidence.independence: This is a proxy, not confirmed by Pulmonx or a direct counterparty. No other source points the same way for Pulmonx specifically.

evidence.text: Inducement-plan hiring slowed. Pulmonx granted 52,300 RSUs to 4 people hired in Q3 2026, against 17 hires and 84,300 RSUs in H1 2026. Sales capacity added in Q3 was small, so the Q4 ramp the guide needs must come from reps hired in H1. Management said those reps take 6-9 months to ramp, which puts them partly productive by Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Inducement-grant releases are boilerplate nobody reads. The signal is ambiguous: H1 hires ramping into Q4 support the guide, while fewer new reps in Q3 limit upside, hence the small size.
evidence.independence: The 6-9 month ramp and 1-year average tenure are from the Q2 call (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2943037). The H1 grant release of 2026-06-01 is a different document from the same company.

evidence.text: Short interest fell from 3.6M shares (2026-04-30) to 0.70M (2026-10-15, 2.54 days to cover), so there is little squeeze fuel behind an upside surprise. The stock gave back from $2.26 (2026-09-01) to $1.975 while still about 55% above its pre-Q2 level.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 +28.8% reaction came when short interest was several times higher.
evidence.why_not_priced: Positioning is the information set itself. This is filed near zero as context, not as an edge.
evidence.independence: MarketBeat shows 1.76% of float and 2.54 days (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/LUNG/short-interest/). The April figure is from the optionsanalysissuite snippet.

evidence.text: Dutch TTF gas rose from EUR 47.83/MWh on 2026-06-01 to EUR 80.77 on 2026-09-11 (+69%), and the November contract was still EUR 76.14 on 2026-10-02. In its Q1 2026 report O-I said Europe's energy costs had stepped up after favourable contracts expired, so Q3 Europe (segment profit $0 in Q1, $6M in Q2) carries a higher energy bill than the July 28 guide may have assumed. That raises the risk of a fourth consecutive cut to the FY2026 $1.0-1.1B EBITDA guide or to the 2027 $1.2-1.3B target.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance cuts drove the last two prints: Q1 2026 cut on European energy costs, -15.53%; Q2 2026 EBITDA guide cut and 2027 target lowered, -15.01%. Q3 2025 (Europe profit +70%) was +14.15%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The +9.9 put skew and the October target cuts (UBS $6, RBC $7) lean the same way. If it were fully priced, the stock would not have rallied +13% over 20 days into the print, and the consensus FY EPS of ~$0.36 on MarketBeat would have been cut. How much of the Q3 spike is hedged is not public, so the size of the hit to the guide is unknown to the market as well.
evidence.independence: Company-level confirmation of energy exposure: Q1 2026 release said Europe segment profit fell on 'a step-up in energy costs following expiration of favorable contracts' (https://app.edgar.tools/filing/812074/0001104659-26-050406/tm2612892d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-04-28). TTF level corroborated by ANSA/soldionline on 2026-10-02 (https://www.soldionline.it/notizie/forex-commodities/gas-perche-e-tornato-sopra-76-euro-il-future-ttf-novembre-298). Macro-to-company transmission is a proxy, because the hedge ratio is not disclosed.

evidence.text: The Q3 adjusted EPS bar of $0.03 (Earnings Whispers) is below Q2's $0.09 and below the H1 run-rate of $0.07 per quarter. In the July 28 release management said adjusted earnings would 'gradually improve over the rest of 2026'. The Americas furnace event was 'substantially resolved in July', $115-120M of Fit to Win savings is expected in H2 (just under half locked in), and new business adds 1-1.5% to volume. If the quarter merely follows the company's own trajectory, it clears the bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 beat with Europe profit +70% bought +14.15%. Q2 2026 EPS miss ($0.09 vs $0.22-0.24) with a guide cut sold -15.01%. Q1 2026 miss ($0.05 vs $0.09) with a cut sold -15.53%. The stock has traded the guide, not the EPS print, on the last two quarters.
evidence.why_not_priced: Analysts appear to have modelled Q3 below Q2 despite the company saying the opposite. The October target cuts (UBS, RBC, Wells) reset expectations lower. If the market believed the company's trajectory, consensus would sit at or above $0.09. The bar has a single source (Benzinga snapshots disagree), and the 40-70% tax rate makes EPS noisy, so the size is capped.
evidence.independence: Company trajectory statements come from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000812074/000110465926087559/tm2621494d1_ex99-1.htm) and the Q2 call (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/OI/Q22026). first_hunter_context.bar: There are two bars. FY2026 company guide (cut 2026-08-10): revenue $600-625M, adjusted net income $115-130M, adjusted EPS $1.34-1.51 (https://s206.q4cdn.com/723382727/files/doc_news/OppFi-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results-Record-Second-Quarter-Revenue-2026.pdf). FY consensus (S&P via stockanalysis, 4 analysts): revenue $611.4M, EPS $1.41, sitting inside the guide (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/opfi/forecast/). The Q3 bar has ONE source: Earnings Whispers, EPS $0.41 on revenue $156.34M (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/OPFI). Q3 sizes are therefore capped small. H1 revenue was $297.05M, so the guide implies H2 revenue of $303-328M, or about $151.5-164M a quarter.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: FINRA short interest, from equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/opfi/shortinterest). Settlement 2026-10-15: 4,283,126 shares, 7.40 days to cover, 5.0% of the 85.2M shares outstanding. Settlement 2026-09-30: 4.32M. Settlement 2026-07-31: 2.40M. The short has risen about 78% since before the August print. Free float is well below 85.2M: Class V was eliminated and every share is now Class A (10-Q cover, 85,208,247 shares at 2026-08-06), but the Schwartz entities hold a large block. The CEO's Form 4 alone shows about 26.9M shares direct plus indirect, so the short is a materially larger share of free float than 5%; I estimate low-to-mid teens, not sourced. No usable skew: the option chain is unusable (ATM spread 100% of mid, total open interest 626, put/call OI 0.35). Tape: -10.5% over 20 days, -52.2% from the 52-week high, 0.4% above the 52-week low.

evidence.text: This is my own arithmetic on primary-document metrics, not a company number. Q3 revenue is more likely $148-154M than the $156.3M single-source bar. Q2 2026 ended with receivables of $440.1M (+0.5% YoY), net originations of $212.0M (-9.3% YoY), retained originations -14.1% and yield of 132.4% (136.1% a year earlier). Q2 revenue of $145.2M implies average receivables of about $439M at that yield. Q3 2025 printed $155.1M revenue only after receivables grew about 10% in the quarter, from $437.8M to $481M, with originations +12.5%. To reach $156M at a 132% yield, average Q3 receivables need to be about $473M. That means roughly 15% quarter-on-quarter book growth while underwriting is being deliberately tightened.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-10 revenue missed ($145.2M against about $156-160M) together with a guide cut, and the stock fell 24.9%. In Q1 2026 (2026-05-07), revenue of $152M with originations down 7% got +1.4%. A revenue miss on its own has not been isolated from guidance in this history.
evidence.why_not_priced: The only Q3 revenue estimate I can find ($156.34M) is above what the Q2 book supports. If the market had marked Q3 down to the book, the published Q3 bar would sit near $150M. Instead the FY consensus ($611.4M) still sits on the guide midpoint, which needs H2 revenue of about $157M a quarter.
evidence.independence: The Q3 2025 comparison comes from a different document: the company's Q3 2025 release, revenue $155.1M, receivables $481M (https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2025/OppFi-Reports-Record-Quarterly-Revenue-Net-Income-and-Adjusted-Net-Income-and-Increases-Full-Year-Guidance/default.aspx). The 8-K presentation confirms the tightening language: 'Deliberate credit tightening and moderated originations' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000073/a2026q2earningspresentat.htm). Against this finding: the $75M term loan drawn 2026-09-15 is earmarked for receivables growth. All of this is an inference from the company's own metrics.

evidence.text: Credit is the line the cut guide rests on, and it was still deteriorating in Q2 despite tightening. Annualised net charge-offs were 52.3% of average receivables (43.5% a year earlier). NCO as a share of revenue was 39.5% (31.9% a year earlier). The fair-value mark on receivables was -$59.0M (-$42.2M a year earlier). On the Q4 2025 call management said summer vintages showed higher defaults, and those charge off in Q3. Q3 2025 printed NCO at 35.1% of revenue. A repeat of about 40% would keep pressure on adjusted net income, but the August guide was set with this credit picture in view.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (NCO 52.3%) came with the guide cut: -24.9%. Q3 2025 (NCO 35.1% of revenue, only modestly higher) came with a guide raise: +3.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the guide was cut on it and the stock is at its 52-week low. What is not public is the Q3 NCO and the delinquency trend under Model 6.1. A stock already pricing worse credit would not have fallen another ~10% over 20 days. Its sign is uncertain, which is why this is sized small and inside the guide.
evidence.independence: Q4 2025 call: summer-vintage defaults were higher (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/oppfi-q4-earnings-call-highlights-185825283.html). This shares the Q2 release and presentation with the revenue finding, but it is a different line (losses, not yield or book).

evidence.text: Enova's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-22) is the only subprime online-lender read that has printed since OppFi last spoke. Consolidated net charge-off ratio fell to 8.1% from 8.5% YoY, originations rose 31%, and management called credit 'stable'. 30+ day delinquency rose to 8.0% from 7.2%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of OPFI reacting to an Enova print.
evidence.why_not_priced: Enova printed after OppFi's last update, and OPFI kept drifting lower (it is down 9.6% in October). That suggests the read-across was not taken. It is a weak transmission: Enova's book is near-prime plus small business, while OppFi lends at about 130% yield to deeper subprime, and Enova's own delinquency rose.
evidence.independence: This is a proxy from a different issuer. OneMain's Q3 was not found (last seen Q2 2026: consumer NCO 7.77% against 7.19% a year earlier, https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/OMF).

evidence.text: Positioning favours a relief move. Short interest built from 2.40M shares (2026-07-31) to 4.28M (2026-10-15), with days to cover up from 2.15 to 7.40 on thin turnover (average daily volume 579k). The stock is 0.4% above its 52-week low, -52% from its high, and at $5.44 trades at about 3.8x the midpoint of the cut FY adjusted-EPS guide ($1.34-1.51).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last print into a heavy drawdown was 2026-03-11 (the stock had made a 12-month low on 2026-03-27 per MarketBeat): -5.9%. Up 5 of 7 prints overall.
evidence.why_not_priced: A short of 7.4 days to cover on a closely held float is a mechanism of its own: a reaffirmed guide forces covering into thin liquidity. If the market saw no squeeze risk, days to cover would not have tripled into the print.
evidence.independence: The price level comes from AAII (2026-10-27): $5.45, -9.6% in October, -47.9% YTD (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/542930-why-oppfi-inc8217s-opfi-stock-is-down-501). The guide comes from the company release.

evidence.text: CEO Todd Schwartz bought in the open market during Q3 itself. He bought 60,000 shares at about $7.13 (Form 4 filed after 2026-08-13), then about 29,600 shares on nine days from 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-14 at $6.91-7.96. That is roughly $650k in total, with the quarter two weeks from closing. The stock is now $5.44, below every purchase price.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior insider-buy cluster in the baseline to compare.
evidence.why_not_priced: The buys are public, but the stock fell about 30% from his last purchase price afterwards. The market has not treated the CEO's in-quarter purchases as information about Q3. If it had, the drawdown to new lows into the print would be hard to explain. The dollar amount is small against his roughly 27M-share stake.
evidence.independence: Other Form 4s in the same cluster: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000090514826004133/form4.xml and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000090514826004056/form4.xml. All are one actor, so this counts as one finding.

evidence.text: The BNCC bank acquisition is still waiting on OCC, Fed and FDIC approval, with a Q4 2026 close expected. Opposition is organised: 18 state attorneys general wrote on 2026-08-07, Senator Warren on 2026-08-14, and more than 120 advocacy groups have asked the regulators to deny it. BNCC stockholders approved the deal on 2026-09-17, and no approval has been reported. The call will update the timeline: a slip into 2027 is the likelier news given the opposition, an approval the upside.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The deal was announced on 2026-04-28 and the following print (2026-05-07) got +1.4%. Deal costs ($7.9M of Q2 transaction expense) were part of the August miss (-24.9%).
evidence.why_not_priced: The opposition is public and part of the overhang. What is not public is the regulators' status. A market expecting a clean Q4 close would not have the stock at a 52-week low with the bank thesis as the bull case.
evidence.independence: The AG coalition letter comes from a different source (https://insurancenewsnet.com/oarticle/attorney-general-raoul-leads-coalition-urging-federal-government-to-deny-opportunity-financial-merger, 2026-08-07). So does Warren (https://www.banking.senate.gov/newsroom/minority/warren-urges-occ-fdic-fed-to-block-a-predatory-lender-from-spreading-nationwide).

evidence.text: The line-of-credit product was the stated cause of the August guide cut. Management said then it would launch with a bank partner in September 2026, already about two months late. I found no launch announcement or press release through 2026-10-27. If it slipped again, the H2 revenue ramp the guide assumes has slipped with it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The prior delay was disclosed with the cut guide on 2026-08-10: -24.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: A quiet launch is plausible: it is a bank-partner product in three new states and might not get a press release. So the absence of an announcement is weak evidence and is sized small. A market confident in the launch would credit the H2 guide, and the FY consensus sits at its midpoint.
evidence.independence: The press-release search for September-October 2026 returned only the earnings-date notice and a conference-participation notice (https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/oppfi-oppfi-announces-its-third-quarter-2026-earnings-conference-call-20261019).

evidence.text: On 2026-09-15 the company drew $75M of a new $100M senior secured multi-draw term loan at a fixed 12.50% (13.50% after the bank deal closes), with a 1.25% OID and 10% semi-annual amortisation. Stated use of proceeds: growth in finance receivables. It replaces the $75M of capacity lost when the GrayRock facility was terminated on 2026-04-15. That adds about $2.3M a quarter of interest from Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No financing-driven reaction in the baseline. A $150M revolver was announced earlier with no isolated move recorded.
evidence.why_not_priced: I asked what the money buys: receivables growth. Nothing corroborates a ramp, since originations were -9.3% YoY in Q2, so I read it as replacement funding at a high fixed cost rather than a demand signal. Its cost reaches the P&L from Q4 and may show in the guide. It is small against $104M of H1 free cash flow.
evidence.independence: The GrayRock termination is in the Q2 presentation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000073/a2026q2earningspresentat.htm).

evidence.text: A regulatory decision on the BNCC/BNC National Bank applications (OCC, Fed, FDIC) is expected around the Q4 2026 close and is unlikely to land inside the window. The opposition makes a delay or conditions more likely than not.

evidence.text: The Dallas office loan ($44.2M principal, risk-rated 4, $6.3M CECL reserve at 6/30) was repaid at about 97% of balance in Q3, with a ~$1.5M discount. SEVN's own DE definition says DE is 'reduced for realized losses on loan investments when amounts are deemed uncollectable ... generally at the time a loan is repaid'. That is about $0.067/sh off DE on 22.4M shares, so reported Q3 DE would land near $0.16-0.19 against the company's $0.23-0.25 guide (the guide was given when management said 'We believe that loan will be paid off' and that the appraisal covered it). The same event releases most of the $6.3M reserve (~$4.8M, ~$0.21/sh) into GAAP net income, so GAAP EPS likely beats while headline DE misses. Net sign negative because this name trades on DE against the $0.28 dividend.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: DE $0.23 against $0.25 consensus and at the low end of the guide; stock -4.73% on the print (baseline) and -4.7% to $7.66 per Simply Wall St. 5 of the last 7 prints were negative. The 2026-10-05 release disclosing the discount traded +1.3% (6.75 -> 6.84), so the market read it as de-risking, not as a DE hit.
evidence.why_not_priced: The discount is public but was never stated in DE terms: the 10-05 release gives no earnings figure and no sell-side Q3 DE number is visible. If the market had mapped it into DE, the 10-05 session would not have closed up, and the Q3 guide would have been visibly reset.
